Subject: Onboarding & PO question for Redwood: AcmeCorp implementation

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. We're ready to kick off the integration work for AcmeCorp and have the signed SOW attached (one-time professional services, $9,500). Procurement here typically issues a PO before payment, but our PM is ready to start the week of May 4 and we're tight on timeline.

Question: can Redwood accept an invoice without a PO for this one-time engagement, or do you require a PO in place before work starts? If a PO is required, can we expedite — we can route a standard PO request internally if needed.

I've attached the onboarding_form_acmecorp.pdf and the SOW (acme_sow_v1.docx). Happy to provide any vendor forms you need.

Best,
Sophie Turner

AcmeCorp

Laura — Acme has a signed SOW for $9,500 and asks whether we can accept an invoice (no PO) so they can start May 4. If a PO is strictly required, do we have a defined exception path for one-off services under $10k? Karthik and I recommend an exception if possible — low risk and accelerates onboarding.

I'll stand by for next steps and can provide the HubSpot deal id if helpful.

Cheers,

Thanks for the ping, Ben. A couple quick notes on process:

- Our standard policy requires a PO for any vendor spend > $5,000. That said, exceptions are possible but require a signed PO exemption request plus Procurement Director approval for values between $5k and $25k.
- To evaluate, we need the vendor W-9 (or tax form), the final signed SOW, and a completed vendor onboarding packet (risk questionnaire / bank remit info). Please share those items and I'll start the exception packet.

If Acme provides the documents today, I can route the exemption to my director for an expedited review (24–48 hours). If approved, Finance will accept an invoice without a PO for this specific SOW and we'll document the exception.

I'll attach the PO exemption form for your reference.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: po_exemption_request.pdf

Quick follow-up — from the account perspective we strongly recommend approving the exception in this case. Rationale:

- One-time professional services, fixed SOW of $9,500 (below typical risk threshold we see for ongoing engagements)
- Vendor provided all required paperwork (W-9, signed SOW, onboarding form)
- Delaying the start will push the client timeline and impact NRR for Q2.

Suggested path: Procurement completes the PO exemption form and routes to Procurement Director + Finance for sign-off. Finance can accept invoice without PO for this SOW if director signs. If Finance wants an additional control, we can require the invoice to reference the exemption document and a GL/cost-center code provided at payment.

Ben — please confirm the start date with Acme after procurement confirms. Laura — can you start the exemption packet? I can escalate to my manager if you need faster routing.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Lead | Redwood Inference

All — following review of the submitted materials, Finance is comfortable with a one-time invoice without a PO for this SOW ($9,500) under the following conditions:

1) Procurement files the signed PO exemption request and stores it in the shared procurement folder (see link).
2) The vendor W-9 and signed SOW are retained with the exemption record.
3) Payment to be made Net 30 on receipt of invoice; invoice must reference the exemption ID and the Redwood GL/cost-center code we provide.

I've attached the signed exemption record for filing and will add the GL code once Karthik confirms the cost center. This is a single-use exception for this SOW only; repeating engagements must follow standard PO flow.

Ben / Karthik — please confirm start date with Acme and forward the invoice to ap-invoices@redwood.com with the exemption ID in the subject line.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
